question.:question/problem: Simplify the trigonometric expression $\frac{\cos^{2} θ\sin^{2} θ + \sin^{4} θ}{\cos θ\sin θ}$.

knowledge_point.title: Simplifying a Rational Expression Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we factor the numerator:

$$
2\cdot\left(\frac{\cos^{2} \phi\sin^{2} \phi + \sin^{4} \phi}{\cos \phi\sin \phi}\right)=2\cdot\left(\frac{\sin^{2} \phi(\cos^{2} \phi+\sin^{2} \phi)}{\cos \phi\sin \phi}\right)
$$

Next, we use the Pythagorean identity to rewrite the expression in the parentheses, and then we simplify the resulting expression as much as possible.

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot\left(\frac{\sin^{2} \phi(\cos^{2} \phi+\sin^{2} \phi)}{\cos \phi\sin \phi}\right) & =2\cdot\left(\frac{\sin^{2} \phi\cdot 1}{\cos \phi\sin \phi}\right) \\ & =2\cdot\left(\frac{\cancel{\sin \phi}\sin \phi}{\cos \phi\cancel{\sin \phi}}\right) \\ & =2\cdot\left(\frac{\sin \phi}{\cos \phi}\right) \\ & =2\tan \phi\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
2\cdot\left(\frac{\cos^{2} \phi\sin^{2} \phi + \sin^{4} \phi}{\cos \phi\sin \phi}\right)=2\tan \phi.
$$
